skill.name: higgsfield-youtube-thumbnail
skill.description: Create truthful YouTube thumbnails and vertical video covers with Higgsfield. Generate controlled variants, preserve referenced identities, refine selected images, and add optional text overlays.
skill.summary: Generate polished video thumbnails with controlled concepts, identity references, focused edits, and optional text overlays.
skill.author: higgsfield-ai

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, JavaScript syntax, or visual-design prose. The remote installer uses an unpinned curl-to-shell command, while local references and Google Fonts create disclosed third-party transfers. No prompt injection or covert exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: The bootstrap runs a mutable remote script directly through sh.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the installer to an immutable commit, download it first, verify a published checksum, and require user confirmation before execution.

remediation.issue: Local face and logo images are automatically uploaded to a third-party service.
remediation.suggestion: Explain the upload destination before submission and request confirmation for sensitive images. Document retention and deletion behavior.

remediation.issue: Text overlays fetch fonts from Google Fonts at render time.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle an approved local font or disclose the request. Provide a local fallback for private or offline workflows.

content.value_statement: Strong thumbnails require clear concepts, readable composition, and truthful visual promises. This skill generates controlled Higgsfield variants and supports focused edits and overlays.
actual_capabilities: Develops truthful thumbnail concepts from a video topic, title, or creative brief.
Generates 16:9, 9:16, or 4:5 images through supported Higgsfield models.
Uses up to three face references and an optional logo in a defined input order.
Creates separate variants for concepts, expressions, and camera directions.
Applies focused expression, background, and rim-light edits to selected results.
Provides five HTML canvas text-overlay presets with native-resolution PNG export guidance.
limitations: Requires the Higgsfield CLI, an authenticated account, network access, and available generation credits.
Uploads local reference images to Higgsfield when they are used for generation.
Cannot guarantee identity accuracy, exact text rendering, or visual quality without inspection.
HTML canvas rendering is required for deterministic overlays, and some edits cannot preserve a 4:5 ratio.

use_cases.title: Launch a YouTube Video
use_cases.description: Create several truthful 16:9 thumbnail concepts with clear focal subjects and strong mobile readability.

use_cases.title: Prepare Vertical Covers
use_cases.description: Generate 9:16 Shorts covers or 4:5 Instagram covers while keeping faces in readable positions.

use_cases.title: Maintain Brand Consistency
use_cases.description: Use face references, logos, controlled variants, and focused edits across a recurring video series.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Thumbnail
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a truthful 16:9 YouTube thumbnail for a video titled "[title]" with one clear subject and no text.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a title and default settings

prompt_templates.title: Create Concept Variants
prompt_templates.prompt: Create four distinct 16:9 concepts for "[topic]" using [face image], while preserving identity and avoiding unsupported claims.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Vertical Cover
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 9:16 Shorts cover for "[topic]" with the face in the upper two-thirds and a two-word overlay.

prompt_templates.title: Direct a Branded Variant Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Create four branded variants for "[topic]" using [face images] and [logo], varying only concept, expression, and camera direction.

output_examples.input: A 16:9 thumbnail for a video about restoring a damaged camera, without text.
output_examples.output: Restoration reveal: a close-up creator holds the damaged camera beside the restored result, with bright separation and no readable text.

output_examples.input: Four Shorts cover concepts about completing a 30-day fitness challenge.
output: Day 30 reveal: determined portrait with a clear final-day badge.
Progression: three vertical stages from day one to day thirty.
Scale contrast: small starting silhouette beside the stronger final pose.
Challenge moment: exhausted expression during the final workout.

output_examples.input: Add the headline "FINAL TEST" to the selected clean thumbnail.
output_examples.output: Neon Lime overlay: FINAL TEST appears in the free lower quarter, away from the face, with a thick dark stroke.

best_practices: Provide the exact video promise, required scene details, target ratio, and approved reference images.
Keep one focal subject and verify that the concept remains readable near 120 pixels wide.
Review every result for truthful claims, identity accuracy, stray text, watermarks, and exact headline spelling.
anti_patterns: Do not imitate a reference thumbnail's identity or exact composition.
Do not request unsupported claims, invented statistics, false screenshots, or misleading outcomes.
Do not combine many subjects, props, labels, and effects into one crowded thumbnail.

faq.question: Which image ratios are supported?
faq.answer: Use 16:9 for standard YouTube thumbnails, 9:16 for Shorts, and 4:5 for Instagram covers.

faq.question: Can the skill preserve a person's identity?
faq.answer: It can use supplied face references and detailed identity instructions, but every result still requires visual review.

faq.question: Can it add headline text?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports deterministic HTML canvas overlays or explicitly requested text baked during image generation.

faq.question: Does it create multiple variants?
faq.answer: Yes. It makes separate generation calls for distinct concepts, expressions, or camera directions, with a maximum of 16 generations.

faq.question: What external services are required?
faq.answer: The workflow requires an authenticated Higgsfield account. Google Fonts is also used by the documented overlay examples.

faq.question: Are local images kept on the device?
faq.answer: No. Local face and logo paths are automatically uploaded to Higgsfield when used as generation inputs.
